generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the psychology you are already studying. Every module you take sets assessments, marks them against criteria, and gives you feedback; the students who understand that cycle, and run it on purpose, are the ones whose lab reports, essays and exam answers improve from one assignment to the next rather than repeating the same mistakes. In psychology you often have more say than you might expect, since courses commonly invite you to help shape assessment, so understanding how it works lets you use that voice well. Treat what follows as being about your own reports, essays and practical work, not about study in the abstract.

The same brief, standard, feedback and next-task cycle runs through professional psychology too. Whether you go into research, clinical training or any applied field, your work is judged against a standard, you receive feedback, and you carry it into what you do next. Learning from that feedback and iterating your practice on the back of it is a habit you keep long after you graduate.
